approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The Home Affairs Bill 2023 would cancel a lease and all related rights over a specific block of land in Yarralumla, Canberra, near Parliament House.
It would do this to protect national security, and the Commonwealth would have to pay compensation if the cancellation takes property without just terms under the Constitution.
The bill would override any other Commonwealth, state or territory law that might otherwise apply to the land or the rights involved.
Terminates a lease and all associated legal interests over Block 26, Section 44 in Yarralumla, Australian Capital Territory.
Makes the Commonwealth liable to pay compensation if the Act results in an acquisition of property other than on just terms.
Provides that the Act has effect despite any other Commonwealth, state or territory law.
The holder of the lease and any person with a legal right, interest or obligation over the land in Block 26, Section 44, Yarralumla.
